title.title: Almost-linear approximation of edit distance
title.subtitle: Claim: edit distance within any fixed factor $1+\varepsilon$ in $N^{1+o(1)}$ expected time

plain: How many typo fixes turn one text into another? Get as close as you like, almost as fast as reading them

beats.text: Exact edit distance fills a quadratic table: kitten to sitting costs 3
Truly subquadratic exact algorithms would refute SETH (Backurs–Indyk, 2015)
Claimed: any fixed accuracy $1+\varepsilon$ in almost-linear time

steps: Split the first string into a tree of pieces
Start from rough cost estimates for every piece
Predict a narrow band where the best alignment runs
Each pass sharpens the estimates; repeat

after.label: Claimed, 24 Sep 2026
after.note: in $N^{1+o(1)}$ expected time, success at least $2/3$

achievement.note: Exact DP still runs below a length threshold the paper calls 'very large'

verify.ourCheck: We did not build the Lean or referee the proof

voice.text: Exact edit distance seems to need quadratic time. Fast methods were only off by a constant.
Rough estimates on a tree of pieces get sharper with every pass.
Claimed: any accuracy, almost linear time.

sources.quote: Backurs-Indyk (STOC 2015): truly subquadratic exact algorithm refutes SETH
Andoni-Nosatzki (FOCS 2020) constant factor (depending on xi) in n^{1+xi}
returns D with ED <= D <= (1+eps)ED with probability >= 2/3, in worst-case expected time N^{1+o(1)}
the algorithm runs exact DP below an accuracy-dependent length threshold the paper calls 'very large'
main theorem formalized: EditApproximation.lean, standard axioms
